text:
Maya: Quick sync — I put together a proposal for "observability acceptance signals" to gate the Console observability launch. Idea is to make launch decisions deterministic, not just subjective. PTAL and raise red flags now.

Sam: love the framing. can you list the specific signals you want?

Maya: sure, draft list: 1) Dashboard coverage: default dashboards for errors/cost/latency present and passing smoke checks. 2) Tracing hooks: top 3 user pathways instrumented (ingest -> route -> render). 3) Error analytics: key error slices identifiable and <X% unexplained. 4) Cost telemetry: token-level cost breakdown available and 1M-token monthly projection under budget. 5) SLOs: P95 latency <200ms on sample traffic and error budget <1% for top routes.

Priya: for "dashboard coverage" what does passing smoke checks mean concretely?

Maya: good call. smoke checks = dashboards load within 2s, panels show non-empty data for last 24h, and at least one alert rule wired to an oncall.

Luca: tracing hooks — we need instrumentation guidelines. I propose a checklist: span at entry/exit, key metadata (customer_id, route, model_id), and sampled traces for slow requests >500ms.

Sam: note: some model-backed routes have dynamic sampling. we should ensure KV cache hits don't blow up trace volume. add guidance: don't trace for cached fast-path unless error.

Hannah: from UX side we should include a "default" dashboard template so non-power-users have a sensible first view. I can mock a three-panel layout: latency, cost per route, top error slices.

Carlos: marketing/customer asks: customers care about cost attribution per-team and per-model. can the telemetry surface both?

Priya: yes — we'll add labels: team_id and model_version tags in metrics pipeline. but that requires a small schema change. I'll scope effort: ~2 dev days + 1 pipeline run.

Janelle: re: enterprise customers — they want exportable audit logs and KMS redaction markers in traces. can that be a must for Private deployments?

Maya: proposal: make KMS/audit logs a hard requirement for Private; keep audit export as a must-have for GA. tracing PII redaction can be a follow-up.

Sam: quick sizing: implementing tracing checklist + dashboard templates + alert wiring ~= 3 engineers x 2 weeks if done in parallel. cost telemetry + schema tags ~= 1.5 weeks. QA + runbooks ~= 1 week.

Luca: rollout plan suggestion: canary at 5% of Console orgs (real traffic), monitor acceptance signals for 48h, if any signal fails we roll back and open a bug with priority. fallback model: route to lightweight fallback UI.

Maya: agreed. Acceptance rule: during canary, all signals must be green for 48h, otherwise block GA. we also include a manual "product go/no-go" checkpoint after canary.

Sam: can we automate signal checks? e.g., a daily job that evaluates the checklist and posts status to #release-war-room and pings owners.

Priya: I can add a job that runs the checklist queries and outputs a pass/fail. example query for error slice presence:

```
count_over_time(error_count{service=\"console\",scope=\"api\"}[24h]) > 0
```
If it returns 0 for a critical route, mark fail.

Hannah: small UX ask — add a health badge in the Console header for admins to see live acceptance status during canary. green/yellow/red.

Carlos: SLO/cost thresholds — we need specific numbers to evaluate. propose: P95 < 200ms, error rate < 1% on top 90% traffic, projected cost per 1M tokens < $25 (hosted). open to debate.

Maya: those numbers look reasonable as starting points. let's mark them as provisional and include a "tolerance" for the canary: 10% slack.

Luca: alerting: any regression that moves P95 above 250ms or error rate >2% should trigger immediate rollback. add runbook link once Sam/QA produce it.

Sam: putting owners: dashboards & alerts = Hannah + Sam, traces = Luca + Sam, cost telemetry = Priya, QA/runbooks = Sam, release automation = Maya + deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: scheduled: observability-acceptance-check job created. runs at 08:00 UTC and on-demand.

Janelle: I'll coordinate with customers chosen for canary (3 early adopters) and confirm data-sharing agreements for telemetry.

Maya: next steps: 1) Priya to implement cost tags & checklist job (ETA 10/3). 2) Sam + Hannah to produce dashboard templates + alerts (ETA 10/7). 3) Luca to finalize tracing checklist and sampling config (ETA 10/5). 4) Maya to schedule canary and customer invites (ETA 10/9). 5) Carlos/Janelle to prep comms and runbooks.

Sam: noted. posting a minimal acceptance checklist doc in Confluence after this thread.

Maya: thanks all. if no objections by EOD I'll convert this into a formal launch gate and add to the roadmap ticket. :thumbsup:
